summary: Listed as a 24.4 m (80 ft) light steel tower with a square cab near Twin Lakes, New Liskeard; no build date, status or site description found.

facts.design: Light steel tower with a square cab
facts.location: West Timiskaming District, ON (firelookout.ca); Twin Lakes, New Liskeard (Canada Lookouts index)

evidence.supports: Light steel tower, 80 ft, with a square cab
evidence.quote: 80-foot light steel tower with a square cab.

evidence.supports: Index places the tower at Twin Lakes, New Liskeard
Register places the tower in West Timiskaming District, ON
Most Ontario towers were erected between the 1920s and the 1950s
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers were under Lands and Forests, which became the MNR in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: By 2013 the Ontario MNR had decided to take down many towers still standing
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these towers still standing.

evidence.supports: Lookouts were used less through the 1960s as aerial spotting and fire-fighting crews took over
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: Only two tower-specific sources: a volunteer index (height and cab) and the firelookout.ca record (location and coordinates, with its Tower Type, Height and Year Built fields all N/A). No build year, status, staffing or site description was found. A firelookout.ca Facebook post about this tower (saying it is believed to still stand) could not be read beyond its title, so it is not cited. The brief's local_unit Timiskaming District matches the register's West Timiskaming District. Height 24.4 m is converted from the index's 80-foot figure.
